thesis: The U.S. economy is dominated by financial services, real estate, and insurance sectors that collectively generate nearly $6.8 trillion in output, but the industry-by-industry revenue ranking reveals deeper structural drivers: banking ($1.57T), real estate ($1.54T), and insurance ($1.53T+) compete at scale with healthcare, energy, and retail.

facts.claim: Finance, real estate, insurance, rental and leasing account for $6.8 trillion in economic output, more than one-fifth of entire U.S. economy.
Commercial banking generated $1,571.4 billion in revenue for 2026, the largest single industry by revenue.
Commercial real estate produced $1,536.2 billion in 2026 revenue despite office vacancy reaching 20.7% in Q2 2025.
Health and medical insurance generated $1,531.2 billion in 2026 revenue, driven by medical cost inflation and declining uninsured rates.
Professional and business services added $4.1 trillion to GDP, the second-largest sector after combined FIRES industries.
Oil and gas extraction remains a top revenue producer at $576.9 billion, with solar power generation as the 4th fastest-growing sub-sector at 19% revenue growth.
